smeGate.notes: No rule has been certified. The generator is internally consistent by construction; real-world causal fidelity is UNVERIFIED. Learner exposure is blocked until every rule carries verdict PASS / REWORD / RETUNE / REMOVE and smeGate.verdict is SIGNED_OFF.

rules.title: Set index = (line address) mod setCount
rules.claim: Consecutive cache lines map to consecutive sets; addresses L apart share a set iff their line indices are congruent mod setCount.
rules.realWorldBasis: Standard bit-sliced set selection for non-hashed caches; matches textbook set-associative indexing.

rules.title: LRU replacement: hit refreshes recency; eviction removes least-recent line
rules.claim: A hit moves the line to MRU position; a miss into a full set evicts the LRU line. Eviction count increments only on capacity pressure.
rules.realWorldBasis: Canonical LRU. Real hardware approximates LRU (pseudo-LRU, adaptive policies); tie-breaking and PLRU differences affect exact miss counts, not directionality.

rules.title: More hot lines than associativity in one set => cyclic thrash
rules.claim: When a cyclic access pattern touches > associativity distinct lines of a single set, every iteration misses because each pass evicts lines later passes need. Set skew becomes extreme; total footprint stays tiny.
rules.realWorldBasis: Textbook conflict-miss mechanism; directionally certain. Exact skew magnitudes are recipe artifacts, not hardware claims.

rules.title: Working set exceeding cache => misses spread across sets with reuse present
rules.claim: Sweeping data larger than the cache yields evenly spread misses; lines have reuse but are evicted before reuse distance closes.
rules.realWorldBasis: Definitional for capacity misses. The reuse-factor threshold that separates 'churn' from 'temporal loss' (<=2.5) is a diagnostic heuristic, not hardware.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: spread misses + low reuse => working-set/capacity family

rules.title: First touch of a line is a miss even in an empty cache
rules.kernel: sim.ts SetAssocLru (any miss to unseen tag)
rules.claim: Fresh-data walks produce near-100% first-touch miss rates regardless of geometry.
rules.realWorldBasis: Definitional for compulsory misses. NOTE: real machines hide some first-touch cost via hardware prefetch; our model accounts for this through the prefetch channel, not the raw counter — see prefetch-next-line rule.

rules.title: Scattered/strided access uses most of each line once => miss rate approaches compulsory floor
rules.kernel: construct.ts (gather-scatter, column-walk recipes); analyze.ts gapPattern classification
rules.claim: Pointer-chase or wide-stride patterns touch few bytes per line; nearly every access misses. Gap-pattern classification (contiguous <=1.2 lines, short-stride <=4, long-stride <=40, else scatter) is a derived heuristic from the mean inter-access gap.
rules.realWorldBasis: Directionally standard (spatial locality loss). The gap thresholds are arbitrary bin boundaries chosen for solver separability — NOT perceptual or hardware boundaries. A learner should not infer that 1.3 vs 1.1 mean-gap is meaningful.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: scatter/long-stride gaps + once-used lines => spatial-locality family

rules.title: Reuse exists but reuse distance exceeds cache => temporal locality loss
rules.claim: Interleaving two large streams preserves per-line reuse but inflates reuse distance past cache size, so lines evict before re-use. Signature: spread misses with reuse factor >1 but ineffective.
rules.realWorldBasis: Standard reuse-distance reasoning. Simplification: single flat cache instead of stack-distance profile.

rules.title: Degree-1 next-line prefetch: one issue per demand miss; useful iff L+1 demanded later
rules.claim: Prefetch usefulness equals the fraction of issued lines whose successor line appears anywhere later in the demand stream. Sequential sweeps approach ~100% useful; scattered streams approach 0%.
rules.realWorldBasis: Real next-line prefetchers behave this way directionally. REAL DEVIATION: usefulness here ignores ORDER (L+1 counted as useful even if demanded before L was missed) and ignores timeliness (prefetch may arrive after demand). Real prefetchers also train/boost degrees; ours never adapts. Consequence: our useful-fraction OVERSTATES real-world effectiveness on mixed streams. Diagnostic heuristics trained ('healthy >=50% useful', 'defeated <35%') are model-relative thresholds, not hardware measurements.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: prefetch audit fraction separates storm/starved from healthy streaming

rules.title: Useful prefetches shorten effective miss penalty by min(0.8, 0.9 x usefulFraction)
rules.claim: Cycle estimate multiplies the flat miss penalty by (1 - hideFactor); useless prefetches add 2 cycles each on top.
rules.realWorldBasis: FICTIONAL COUPLING CONSTANT: real penalty reduction depends on memory-level parallelism, timing overlap, and queue occupancy — none modeled. The 0.9/0.8 numbers encode 'mostly helpful, capped' intuition only. Direction (more useful prefetch => faster) is safe; magnitudes are not hardware claims. Do not let any UI text quote cycle counts as physical.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: more useful prefetching => faster; disabling prefetch helps only when prefetching was hurting

rules.title: Every miss costs 120 cycles; coherence transfer costs 90 cycles
rules.claim: Additive stall accounting: baseCpi x accesses + hits x 0 + misses x 120 + transfers x 90 (+ prefetch bus cost).
rules.realWorldBasis: FICTIONAL CONSTANTS: real penalties vary by level hit in (L2/L3/DRAM), row-buffer state, contention, and overlap (MLP). Flat constants preserve ordering between worlds but make absolute cycle numbers meaningless. Slowdown RATIOS remain directionally defensible within one world's baseline comparison.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: misses dominate slowdown; fewer misses => proportionally faster (ratio reasoning, not absolute cycles)

rules.title: Writer alternation on shared lines produces cross-core invalidations; no protocol states
rules.claim: Each write to a line last written by the other core counts as one cross-core invalidation; contended-line count and local writes tracked alongside. Same-word conflicts counted independently at word granularity.
rules.realWorldBasis: Ledger abstraction over MESI-family protocols. Directionally sound: alternating writers on a shared line DO force ownership transfers. MISSING: upgrade/invalidate distinctions, write-broadcast policies, directory vs snoop latency differences, false sharing via DMA/peripheral. Same-word tracking is the true/false-sharing discriminator and mirrors how perf tooling (e.g. c2c-style analysis) attributes HITM events.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: cross-core traffic present + high same-word share => true sharing; low share => false sharing

rules.title: Same-word conflicts > 80% of cross-core invalidations => classify as TRUE sharing
rules.claim: True sharing (both cores writing the SAME word) shows mostly same-word conflicts; false sharing (different words, one line) shows mostly different-word conflicts. Threshold 0.8 separates them in generated worlds.
rules.realWorldBasis: Directionally defensible attribution heuristic mirroring HITM-style analysis. CAVEAT: real workloads mix both modes on the same line; a hard 0.8 boundary does not exist in reality. Trained heuristic is safe ONLY for clean-mode cases; learners should be told real traces are messier.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: same-word share decides which sharing pathology

rules.title: Two-level hierarchy: per-level miss rates computed as independent runs over the same stream
rules.claim: L1 and L2 statistics come from separate simulations, like reading separate hardware counter groups. No inclusion/exclusion policy between levels.
rules.realWorldBasis: Matches how real per-level counters are READ (independent domains), but real hierarchies couple: L2 accesses = f(L1 misses), inclusion forces evictions downward. Our L2 miss counts understate real ones for inclusive designs. Hierarchy-mismatch worlds rely on footprint-vs-L1-size reasoning, which survives the simplification; absolute L2 rates do not.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: working set near/above a level's size => misses migrate to that level

rules.title: Slowdown measured against a known-good twin workload, not a saved profile
rules.claim: Each world embeds a healthy variant of the same workload shape; slowdown = regressed cycles / benign cycles. Baseline miss rate typically 3–7%.
rules.realWorldBasis: Methodological simplification presented as fact: real regression triage compares against historical profiles of THE SAME binary, not a synthetic twin. Pedagogically this trains correct before/after reasoning but should be disclosed as a lab artifact — real baselines drift (data changes, load changes) and that difference matters in practice.
rules.diagnosticHeuristicTrained: compare current against a known-good reference before concluding regression

rules.title: Timeline windows share cache state; cold-start pollution affects early windows only
rules.claim: Eight sequential windows over one continuous stream; window boundaries do not reset cache state. Phase labels attach windows to workload phases when multiple phases exist.
rules.realWorldBasis: Correct for continuous profiling. Window SIZE (stream/8) is arbitrary; real profilers use time slices. Phase-window alignment in phase-change worlds assumes phases align to stream fractions — a recipe property, slightly idealized vs real phase detection.

notModeled: TLB / page-table walk effects (explicitly omitted rather than fake-countered)
store buffering / memory disambiguation / OoO MLP overlap
bus contention feedback between concurrent misses and prefetches
MESI protocol state machine (ledger abstraction instead)
cache hashing (slice/hash-indexed real caches defeat simple bit-slicing)
sampling noise in counters (field scaffolded, deliberately disabled)
